items.explanation: Single-invention explanations overreach: the bulb was useless without generators, wiring, and stations like Pearl Street, and urbanization was already underway before 1879. The bulb was widely adopted. Edison's Menlo Park was team-based, and the infrastructure need is visible in the Pearl Street photographs. Electricity eventually displaced gas lighting.
items.fact_source: u6.md §The story — Edison's light bulb (1879); scope-of-inference reasoning — flagged for audit

option_explanations.A: The bulb was adopted in cities across the country.
option_explanations.B: Correct. The claim overreaches: the bulb needed a whole system, and cities predated it.
option_explanations.C: Menlo Park was team-based, and the bulb plainly required infrastructure.
option_explanations.D: Electricity eventually won out over gas lighting.

options: (A) the light bulb was never actually adopted in any American city at all, remaining a mere laboratory curiosity for decades
(B) the bulb required an entire system — generators, wires, stations — and cities were already growing before it arrived
(C) Edison worked entirely alone in his laboratory, so no larger supporting system was ever needed
(D) gas lighting remained cheaper than electricity forever and never lost its lead in any city

items.explanation: The portrait is John D. Rockefeller. Standard Oil grew by buying rival refineries — horizontal integration, combining competitors at the same stage. Vertical integration (owning every stage from wells to sales) was Carnegie's steel strategy, not Rockefeller's. No government made Standard Oil a sole legal supplier. Rockefeller opposed unions; he did not organize them.
items.fact_source: u6.md §Key terms — Vertical / horizontal integration — buying out rivals (Rockefeller) + §The story — Standard Oil, 1870 + PD portrait, 1880 (stimulus)

option_explanations.A: Owning every stage from wells to retail is vertical integration — Carnegie's steel method, not Rockefeller's.
option_explanations.B: No government granted Standard Oil a legal monopoly.
option_explanations.C: Correct. Standard Oil dominated by buying out competing refineries: horizontal integration.
option_explanations.D: Rockefeller fought unions; he did not build them.

options: (A) owning every stage from oil wells to retail sales — vertical integration
(B) winning government contracts as the sole legal supplier
(C) buying out competing refineries — horizontal integration
(D) organizing oil workers into a single national union
items.stem: The businessman in this 1880 portrait built his fortune in the oil business. The company he founded, Standard Oil (1870), came to dominate oil refining chiefly through which strategy?
